# HLT-C9 extraction notes (A2)

Text: pdftotext -layout of the JSTOR PDF, saved in _text/HLT-C9.txt. Page numbers are the journal's printed pages (60-72). Quotes are verbatim except that the text layer's "G" for "<" and "V" for em dash are restored; "[...]" marks omissions. Figure 1 (service-level scores) is an image; its values are not in the text layer and were not read.

## Rows proposed
- findings: 22 (N 12, Q 10). transformations: 5 (all crossing strands). claims: 18. relations: 7 (covers 7, backs 0, clashes 0). decisions: header only.
- Headline scope: structured abstract Results, Conclusion and Practice Implications (p.60-61), and the closing Practice Implications section (p.70-71), which is the article's conclusions/recommendations section (there is no separate Conclusions heading). The Discussion (p.69-70) is not headline; it is used only under rule 7.
- No research-agenda sentence appears in the headline sections; the Discussion's "Future work could consider..." (p.70) and "Further research would be required..." (p.69) were not extracted (rule 6).

## Look at first
1. C7 (barriers) proposed as joint (fit confirm) under rule 7. The abstract lists four barriers from the interviews. At p.68 the self-interest barrier is argued with survey results: "Consistent with the quantitative findings that showed significant differences in relational coordination across service focus area [...] interviewees expressed that being a provider of direct patient care could be a challenge to collaboration. This is consistent with lower MCDPH domain scores in frequent communication (2.84), shared knowledge (2.88), and shared goals (3.12)." F2, F7, F8 were therefore added to rests_on. If A1 limits rests_on to the interview findings (precedent: HLT-C15 C19, flagged but not added), C7 is Q only.
2. C10 (structured activities to increase shared knowledge and mutual respect) proposed as joint (fit expand) under rule 7. Discussion p.69: "Findings from the relational coordination survey suggest that the department has relatively higher levels of mutual respect [...] compared to its shared knowledge and frequency of communication. To the extent that department leadership seeks to improve relational coordination, these latter areas may offer opportunity" (F6, F7). Discussion p.70: cloud meetings "are unique given their ability to influence changes in virtually every relational coordination domain"; Results p.64: clouds "provided an opportunity for problem-solving communication, shared knowledge, and mutual respect" (F10). Expand rather than confirm: the survey locates the gap, the interviews name the means. Note that "increase [...] mutual respect" sits awkwardly with mutual respect being the highest domain (F6). Without rule 7, rests_on is empty (rule 2) and C10 is not joint.
3. Joint count: 2 (C7, C10) as proposed; 1 or 0 depending on points 1 and 2. A possible third: C9 (senior management support) has empty rests_on (rule 2); the Discussion p.69 places "deliberate managerial attention may be needed" right after "Population-focused services had varying levels of relational coordination" (F9), but without a marker, so F9 was not added.
4. Themes counted (F18-F20). Tables 3 and 4 count interviewees per theme, and the major themes were selected by "a natural cut point" in frequency (p.63). The counts are registered as N findings made from the Q themes (crosses_strand yes); their roots are Q only, so they do not create joint claims. C17 rests on the count ("Demonstrated by the number of staff who mentioned this strategy") and is single-strand after tracing. C6 and C7 could also take F19/F20; this would not change the joint count.
5. Rule 12 transformations (F21, F22). Interview themes compared across services with higher vs lower relational coordination scores (Hypothesis 3). These findings root in both strands, but no headline claim rests on them: the Hypothesis 3 result ("We found limited evidence of heterogeneous barriers and facilitators to collaboration based on the service's level of coordination", p.69) appears only in the Discussion. The Discussion's "potentially novel theme" that higher-scoring services "now knew what they had not known" (p.69-70) restates F21 and was not registered separately.
6. C2 versus the reported test. The abstract says clinical services were significantly lower "than population-focused services (p < .01)"; the Results test compares curative services with all other types (2.64, p < .01), and population health services (3.17) were not significantly different from other groups (F5). C3 ("individually focused" lower than population-focused) includes preventive individual services (3.06), for which no difference was found. Both claims rest on F4 and F5; the wording overstates the reported comparison.
7. C4 "high levels of mutual respect": the domain score is 3.35 on a 1-5 scale (just above the midpoint), the highest of the seven domains. Reliability is lower for shared knowledge (alpha .57) and frequency (alpha .44) (p.63), the two domains used for C5 and C10.
8. Covers relations. R1, R2 rest on the abstract's sentence structure (general result followed by its specification). R3-R6 apply rule 2 (abstract summary of the body). R7 (C10 covers C17) is the weakest: the abstract does not name the cloud meetings. C8 has both rests_on (rule 7, Discussion p.69 on known vs novel factors) and covers relations; A1 may keep only one.
9. No backs proposed: Practice Implications sentences follow one another without markers (C12 then C13 "may be undervalued", then C14 "infrastructure"; C11 then C3). C12 opens with "However" after C3: a qualification both survive (rule 4), no clash.
10. C16 rests on F12 (culture "purposefully fostered by department leaders"). The supporting sentence "The director repeatedly expressed a priority for increased collaboration through reorganization of programs and colocating offices" (p.70) gives no data source; it was not registered as a finding.

## Design-level interface points (rules 9, 13)
- Survey and interview responses were "linked, and all analyses were performed at the public health service level" (p.63). The survey instrument is the existing validated relational coordination tool; no instrument was built from the interviews and no rating panel was used.
- Services were classified into four focus categories by target population (Table 1, p.63). This classification defines the groups for the N comparisons (F2-F5) and for several Q comparisons by focus area (e.g. culture mentioned by "nearly every interviewee working in a population-focused service", p.65). It is a categorical coding of service descriptions, not a registered finding; comparisons by focus area were not treated as rule 12 transformations because the groups are not defined by a quantitative measure.

## Other
- Findings registered as main results but not in any rests_on: F1, F9, F13 (only via C6/C8), F17 (only via C7), F19, F20, F21, F22.
- C11, C13, C14, C18 have empty rests_on (no finding cited).
- Limitations stated by S1 (p.70): self-reported data, one department, leadership and long-tenured respondents only, no outcome measure.
